title: The Curse of Knowing
logline: A seeker who has spent a lifetime refusing every imposed destiny finally chooses to be chosen—and receives the curse of knowing every consequence before it arrives.
sources: User creative direction: choosing to be chosen and gifted with the curse of knowing

metadata.creative_question: What does it mean to choose the fate that chooses you?
metadata.protagonist_principle: The gift is not omniscience; it is involuntary consequence-awareness.
metadata.visual_signature: signal-punk dossier fused with scarlet occult anime

characters.name: The Seeker
goals: discover whether consent can survive prophecy
protect others from consequences only they can see
fears: being chosen as a vessel rather than a person
knowing the exact moment someone will betray them
wounds: every authority figure called obedience a gift
they were praised only when useful
belonging was always offered as a contract
contradictions: they demand freedom while secretly wanting a fate strong enough to hold them
they resent prophecy yet keep trying to prevent it
they fear being known but cannot stop knowing everyone else
visual_anchors: short black hair with one crimson-white streak
left eye reflecting branching red futures
right hand wrapped in ritual thread
small broken halo sigil at the throat
long charcoal coat with scarlet lining
silver divination knife worn as a pendant

characters.name: The Choosing
goals: end the cycle of unwilling vessels
make the bearer witness the cost of every possible mercy
fears: being chosen only out of desperation
a bearer who knows everything except why they stayed
wounds: it has been treated as a weapon for centuries
every former bearer blamed the curse for their own decisions
contradictions: it wants consent but engineers irresistible invitations
it reveals consequences to prevent cruelty while creating paralysis
it calls itself a gift because it cannot bear being called a wound
visual_anchors: faceless crimson silhouette behind translucent ritual glass
many thin hands arranged like a compass
voice represented by angular radio glyphs
halo made of broken clock faces
never fully occupies the same panel as the Seeker

locations.name: The Threshold Archive
locations.description: A ruined observatory-library where rejected destinies are catalogued as living red threads.
sensory_motifs: red thread tightening around forgotten names

locations.name: The City of Almosts
locations.description: A nocturnal city made from futures that nearly happened, where every alley displays a different version of the Seeker.

lore.title: The Law of Consenting Fate
lore.statement: A destiny can call your name, but it cannot become yours until you answer knowingly.

lore.title: The Curse of Knowing
lore.statement: The bearer sees the most probable consequence of each meaningful choice, but never receives the reason a choice remains worth making.

lore.title: The Mercy of Uncertainty
lore.statement: Unknown futures remain alive; every certainty the curse reveals collapses one branch of possibility.

evidence.label: The red thread
evidence.description: A living thread that tightens around the wrist whenever the Seeker approaches a decision they are avoiding.
evidence.consequence: Cutting it transfers one known consequence into someone else's future.

evidence.label: The broken halo
evidence.description: A throat sigil composed of seven incomplete arcs, one for each former bearer.
evidence.consequence: A new arc appears whenever the Seeker chooses despite knowing the cost.

evidence.label: The unwritten door
evidence.description: A door in the Threshold Archive with no predicted future behind it.
evidence.consequence: The curse cannot see beyond it, making it the only place where genuine choice remains possible.

relationships.tension: The Seeker wants to know whether the Choosing loves them or merely needs them.
relationships.history: The Choosing has appeared in every dream since childhood but never completed the invitation.

relationships.tension: The Seeker cannot distinguish intuition from a future already shown.
relationships.history: Each prevented disaster creates a new reason to doubt the prevention.

edges.notes: The only future the curse cannot precompute.
The gift becomes a curse when certainty replaces consent.

events.title: Refusal at the Threshold
events.summary: The Seeker rejects the invitation because the curse shows them every version of themselves who accepts.

events.title: The Choice to Be Chosen
events.summary: After watching a future in which refusal destroys someone else, the Seeker returns and consents without asking what they will become.

events.title: The Gift Opens
events.summary: The Seeker receives the Curse of Knowing and sees consequences branching from every heartbeat in the room.

events.title: Mercy Is a Blind Spot
events.summary: The Seeker discovers that the curse cannot see an act done without the desire to control its result.

events.title: The Known Ending
events.summary: The Seeker sees their own death, refuses to prevent it, and chooses to spend the remaining certainty making one other person free.

scene_contracts.purpose: Establish that refusal is an active choice, not cowardice.
scene_contracts.visual_motif: a hand withdrawing from a door while the red thread remains extended
continuity_notes: The throat sigil has six arcs before consent.

scene_contracts.purpose: Make consent the protagonist's act of authorship.
scene_contracts.visual_motif: the Seeker steps toward the hand that has been waiting
continuity_notes: The Seeker says yes before the curse explains the terms.
The seventh halo arc appears only after the answer.

scene_contracts.purpose: Show knowing as sensory overload rather than generic power.
scene_contracts.visual_motif: one room fractured into red translucent futures
continuity_notes: Keep the left eye as the future eye.
Every branch must retain the same identity anchors.

scene_contracts.purpose: Introduce the loophole: mercy survives when control is relinquished.
scene_contracts.visual_motif: a blank panel where the curse expects an answer
continuity_notes: The blankness is intentional and must not be filled with decorative noise.

scene_contracts.purpose: Resolve the premise by choosing meaning after certainty.
scene_contracts.visual_motif: the Seeker cuts the red thread only after giving it to another free hand
continuity_notes: The final image is not victory; it is an open future.
Preserve the broken halo as a completed but imperfect mark.

shots.camera: high wide angle through observatory glass
shots.action: The Seeker stands before the unwritten door while red threads map rejected futures.
shots.dialogue: I refuse to be grateful for a cage.

shots.camera: low angle on the hand and throat sigil
shots.action: The Seeker accepts the offered hand.
The room splits into hundreds of consequence branches.
The curse reaches toward a blank future and finds no image.
The Seeker places the red thread in another person's open hand.
shots.dialogue: Knowing is not the same as owning.

open_questions: Is consent possible when every alternative is shown?
